name: The Old Ksar
tagline: The fortified earthen village on the hill
description: The historic UNESCO ksar itself, a cluster of packed-mud kasbahs climbing the hillside above the Ounila River. Reached on foot across stepping stones or the footbridge, its lanes wind past crenellated towers to a granary with sweeping views. A handful of families and shops remain among the film-famous walls.
pros: Breathtaking earthen architecture and UNESCO heritage
World-famous film location with unforgettable views
Magical light at sunrise and sunset
cons: Almost no wifi or modern services
Steep, uneven paths and a river crossing

name: Modern Village (Near Riverbank)
tagline: Guesthouses and terraces facing the ksar
description: The living village on the near bank of the Ounila, where most guesthouses, riads, and terrace restaurants cluster with the old ksar in full view across the water. This is where visitors actually sleep, eat, and rest, offering the best available wifi, hospitality, and easy walking access to the historic site.
pros: Walkable to the ksar and river crossing
Best concentration of guesthouses and restaurants
Terrace views of the illuminated ksar
cons: Very tourism-dependent with few local amenities

name: Ouarzazate
tagline: The regional town and film-studio hub
description: The provincial town about 30 minutes away, home to Atlas Film Studios, the Taourirt Kasbah, an airport, banks, and proper services. Ouarzazate is the practical base for anyone needing reliable connectivity, shopping, or transport connections, and it makes a comfortable launch point for exploring the wider south.
bestFor: Remote workers, longer stays, service access
pros: Better wifi, banks, ATMs, and shops
Atlas Film Studios and Taourirt Kasbah to explore
Airport and bus links to the rest of Morocco
cons: Lacks the drama of the ksar itself

name: Skoura Palm Grove
tagline: Oasis kasbahs on the road east
description: A lush palm oasis roughly an hour east of Ait Benhaddou, dotted with historic kasbahs including the celebrated Amridil. Skoura offers tranquil guesthouses set among palms and gardens, a green counterpoint to the desert, and a natural first stop along the Valley of the Roses and Draa Valley routes.
pros: Beautiful palm oasis and historic kasbahs
Gateway to the Draa Valley and Roses route
cons: Spread out and needs a car
Minimal services and no nomad scene
